# Dark-Matter IDEAS — 10,000+ Feature & Technique Ideas

> A brainstorm bank for making Dark-Matter's Hunt agent better than elite human bug-bounty hunters
> and Infinity AI best-in-class. Generated 2026-10-03 by 10 parallel ideation workers (one per
> capability group), then deduplicated and globally numbered.
>
> **Total ideas: 10,004** — each one line: `NNNNN. **Title** — one-sentence description`
> stating the concrete mechanism and why it matters. Raw input: 10,000 lines across 10 part files
> (`ideas/part-01` … `part-10`); removed 8 exact duplicates and 0 near-duplicates.
> Focus: what elite human hunters do that machines don't — automated or done better. Professional English.

## A. Subdomain & asset discovery

00001. **Certificate-transparency substring watch** — monitor CT logs for substrings of the target brand (typosquats, dev/staging prefixes) and auto-queue new hosts for takeover checks within 60 seconds of issuance.
00002. **Precertificate SCT timestamp mining** — harvest pre-certificates from CT logs before the final cert is issued to discover hosts that exist minutes to hours before they go live and probe them in that pre-launch window.
00003. **CT dev-prefix rotation tracking** — detect naming patterns like dev1, dev2, staging-blue in CT logs and predict the next rotation slot to pre-enumerate future environments.
00004. **Typosquat brand-pair generation** — generate keyboard-adjacent, homoglyph, and transposed variants of the target brand, query CT logs for any certificates, and flag squat domains that mimic the target.
00005. **Certificate SAN overlap clustering** — group certificates whose Subject Alternative Names share two or more hosts with the target to reveal sibling infrastructure the target never advertises.
00006. **Wildcard-certificate parent probing** — when a wildcard cert for *.example.com appears, systematically probe common labels plus wordlist-derived names to enumerate the wildcard's actual coverage.
00007. **Expired-cert host resurrection list** — collect hosts from expired certificates for the target org and re-probe them, since expired certs often mark forgotten assets that still respond.
00008. **CT log issuer anomaly flagging** — flag certificates for target domains issued by unexpected CAs or via ACME on unusual schedules, since rogue issuance often reveals attacker or devops side-infrastructure.
00009. **NSEC zone-walk automation** — walk DNSSEC-signed zones via NSEC chain traversal to enumerate every signed name without brute force.
00010. **NSEC3 hash-crack walking** — collect NSEC3 hashes via iterative queries and crack them with optimized wordlists to enumerate names in opt-out-disabled zones.
00011. **NSEC3PARAM salt-harvesting dictionary** — extract NSEC3PARAM salt and iteration counts to build targeted hash lists that make offline NSEC3 cracking feasible at scale.
00012. **AXFR over TCP fallback probing** — attempt zone transfers over plain TCP on every authoritative nameserver, including non-standard ports, since misconfigured secondaries still leak full zones.
00013. **AXFR over TLS/DoT attempt** — probe DNS-over-TLS port 853 for zone-transfer acceptance, which admins secure differently from port 53.
00014. **AXFR over DoH endpoints** — test discovered DNS-over-HTTPS endpoints for AXFR-style responses or zone-dump behavior behind misconfigured HTTPS DNS gateways.
00015. **ANY-query meta-record mining** — issue ANY queries against authoritative servers to collect HINFO, TXT, and legacy record types that reveal hostnames and internal naming.
00016. **DNS NOTIFY-triggered capture** — listen for unsolicited NOTIFY patterns and zone serial increments to time enumeration right after zone updates when new hosts appear.
00017. **HTTPS record (SVCB) alias harvesting** — query HTTPS/SVCB records to extract alpn, port, ipv4hint, ipv6hint, and target aliases that map hidden service endpoints.
00018. **SVCB echconfig extraction** — parse ECH configs from HTTPS records to identify backend service aliases used for encrypted-client-hello fronting.
00019. **ALPN record service inference** — enumerate advertised ALPN protocols per host to infer which services (h2, h3, custom) run behind each name without port scanning.

## B. Port/service/fingerprinting innovations

00335. **Banner-ordering differential probes** — send identical probes with reordered options/headers and fingerprint services by how response ordering changes, distinguishing implementations behind identical banners.
00336. **Error-message differential fingerprinting** — trigger controlled errors (bad method, long URI, malformed headers) and fingerprint servers by exact error text and status-code choices.
00337. **HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame fingerprinting** — fingerprint HTTP/2 stacks by their SETTINGS frame values and order, which vary by server and version.
00338. **HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE behavior profiling** — profile flow-control window behavior to distinguish CDN edge stacks from origins.
00339. **HTTP/3 QUIC handshake fingerprinting** — fingerprint QUIC stacks by version negotiation and transport-parameter ordering.
00340. **JA3 TLS client-hello cataloging** — catalog server-selected cipher suites across JA3 variants to fingerprint TLS terminators.
00341. **JA4/JA4H HTTP fingerprinting** — apply JA4/JA4H fingerprints to server responses to identify CDN and WAF layers.
00342. **JA4S server-hello fingerprinting** — fingerprint TLS servers by their ServerHello extensions and ordering.
00343. **TLS certificate-transparency timing analysis** — correlate certificate issuance timing with deployment events to fingerprint automated vs manual PKI.
00344. **SNI-based virtual-host discovery** — iterate SNI values on one IP to enumerate co-hosted TLS virtual hosts without DNS.
00345. **ALPN negotiation mapping** — test ALPN protocol lists per port to map which services (h2, h3, mqtt, custom) each endpoint offers.

## D. API discovery & testing (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket)

01001. **Swagger UI hidden path sweep** — probe /v3/api-docs, /swagger.json, /openapi.yaml and 40+ vendor-specific doc variants because exposed specs hand attackers the full route map for free.
01002. **FastAPI docs exposure check** — test /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json on every host since FastAPI serves interactive documentation by default unless explicitly disabled.
01003. **Spring Boot actuator enumeration** — walk /actuator, /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump and mapped sub-paths because actuator endpoints frequently leak config, beans and heap memory.
01004. **Postman public workspace harvesting** — query Postman's public API for collections mentioning the target brand since developers publish request collections containing live endpoints and sample tokens.
01005. **AsyncAPI spec discovery** — hunt for asyncapi.json/yaml and EventCatalog portals because event-driven APIs document WebSocket and message topics attackers can subscribe to.
01006. **WSDL endpoint discovery** — probe /service?wsdl, /soap and .asmx variants since legacy SOAP services hide behind modern frontends with verbose operation listings.
01007. **WADL file probing** — request application.wadl and /wadl paths because Jersey/JAX-RS apps expose machine-readable resource listings there.
01008. **OData metadata extraction** — fetch /$metadata on suspected OData services since it enumerates every entity set, function import and navigation property.
01009. **OData batch endpoint test** — probe /$batch for multipart batch support because batching lets attackers bundle many operations past per-request rate limits.
01010. **GraphQL introspection enablement check** — send a __schema query to /graphql and aliases since enabled introspection dumps the entire type system in one response.
01011. **GraphQL field-suggestion bypass** — submit misspelled field names to trigger didYouMean suggestions because suggestion engines leak real field names when introspection is off.
01012. **GraphQL error-based schema inference** — feed malformed selections and parse validation errors since error text reveals valid types, fields and argument names.
01013. **GraphQL __typename mapping sweep** — query __typename across unions and interfaces because it enumerates concrete types without full introspection.
01014. **GraphQL GET-method variant test** — replay POST queries as GET with ?query= since GET-based GraphQL is CSRF-able and often logged in proxies.
01015. **GraphQL playground exposure scan** — probe /playground, /graphiql and /voyager because in-browser IDEs ship with introspection and query history enabled.
01016. **GraphQL persisted-query hash guessing** — test Automatic Persisted Queries with sha256 of common query strings since predictable hashes let attackers execute allowlisted operations.
01017. **GraphQL persisted-query version abuse** — flip version fields in extensions.persistedQuery because version confusion can downgrade hash verification.
01018. **GraphQL query batching probe** — send arrays of queries in one request since batching multiplies brute-force and enumeration throughput.
01019. **GraphQL alias overloading test** — stack dozens of aliased identical fields because aliasing amplifies single-request data extraction.
01020. **GraphQL directive fuzzing** — fuzz @include/@skip with non-boolean values since directive mishandling can bypass field-level gating.
01021. **GraphQL fragment cycle test** — submit self-referencing fragments because cyclic fragments can cause expensive resolver loops.
01022. **GraphQL depth-limit measurement** — nest selections incrementally to find the cutoff since missing depth limits enable deeply nested resource exhaustion.
01023. **GraphQL cost-analysis probing** — craft high-multiplier list queries to infer whether the server computes query cost before execution.
01024. **GraphQL federation _service probe** — query _service { sdl } because federated gateways expose the full composed supergraph schema.
01025. **GraphQL federation _entities abuse** — call _entities with crafted representations since entity resolution can reach subgraph objects directly.
01026. **Subgraph direct-access discovery** — extract subgraph URLs from supergraph SDL and hit them directly because subgraphs often skip gateway-level authorization.
01027. **Federation key-field extraction** — parse @key directives from SDL since key fields reveal the exact identifiers needed for cross-subgraph object references.
01028. **Schema-stitching vs federation fingerprint** — compare _service responses and header behavior because stitching gateways expose different metadata surfaces than Apollo federation.
01029. **gRPC server reflection probing** — call grpc.reflection.v1alpha.ServerReflection since reflection returns every service, method and proto descriptor.
01030. **gRPC reflection-disabled proto hunt** — search for .proto files and descriptor sets on web roots because teams disable reflection but leave protos publicly downloadable.
01031. **gRPC health-check protocol probe** — call grpc.health.v1.Health/Check for known service names since health responses confirm which services actually run.
01032. **gRPC-web support detection** — send gRPC-web framed requests with content-type application/grpc-web because gRPC-web endpoints are reachable from browsers and often CORS-misconfigured.
01033. **gRPC transcoding discovery** — test REST-style paths against gRPC backends since transcoding proxies translate HTTP/JSON to gRPC and may skip method-level checks.
01034. **gRPC error-detail leakage analysis** — trigger INVALID_ARGUMENT and parse google.rpc.Status details because rich error models leak field constraints and internal codes.
01035. **gRPC metadata leakage check** — inspect response trailers and headers since servers often reflect internal metadata like service versions and backend hosts.
01036. **gRPC deadline abuse test** — set extreme deadlines/timeouts because deadline handling differences can leave server-side work running after client disconnect.
01037. **gRPC max-message-size probing** — send incrementally larger messages to map limits since oversized-message handling reveals DoS thresholds and parser behavior.
01038. **Proto field-number guessing** — send unknown field numbers and observe tolerance because lenient parsers accept guessed fields that strict schemas would reject.
01039. **gRPC status-to-HTTP mapping analysis** — compare status codes across transports since inconsistent mappings leak whether an endpoint is native REST or transcoded.
01040. **gRPC keepalive behavior probe** — open idle streams with keepalive pings because keepalive policies reveal connection-lifecycle assumptions attackers can exploit.
01041. **WebSocket handshake fuzzing** — mutate Origin, Sec-WebSocket-Protocol and extensions during upgrade since handshake validation gaps allow cross-origin socket hijacking.
01042. **WebSocket token-in-URL detection** — flag ws:// URLs carrying ?token= or ?auth= because URL tokens leak into proxy logs, browser history and Referer headers.
01043. **WebSocket subprotocol negotiation test** — offer graphql-ws vs subscriptions-transport-ws alternately since servers may accept deprecated protocols with weaker auth.
01044. **WebSocket path fuzzing** — brute-force /ws, /socket.io, /realtime, /cable, /graphql-ws and framework defaults because socket endpoints rarely appear in REST docs.
01045. **Socket.IO namespace enumeration** — connect to guessed namespaces like /admin and /notifications since namespaces partition privilege and some lack auth.
01046. **Socket.IO event-name brute force** — emit common event names and watch for non-error responses because unlisted events often trigger privileged handlers.
01047. **Socket.IO polling fallback abuse** — force long-polling transport because the polling endpoint may enforce different auth than the WebSocket upgrade.
01048. **ActionCable channel enumeration** — subscribe to guessed channel names since Rails ActionCable channels frequently skip authorization on subscribe.
01049. **SignalR hub-method enumeration** — call /negotiate then invoke common hub methods because SignalR hubs expose server methods callable by any connected client.
01050. **SignalR negotiate analysis** — parse connectionToken and availableTransports from /negotiate since token format reveals session binding strength.
01051. **STOMP-over-WebSocket topic sweep** — SUBSCRIBE to wildcard and guessed destinations because STOMP brokers often allow subscribing to other users' queues.
01052. **MQTT-over-WebSocket topic brute force** — subscribe to # and + wildcards since MQTT ACLs are frequently misconfigured to allow broad subscriptions.
01053. **SockJS info endpoint probe** — request /info on SockJS prefixes because the info response discloses websocket support, origins and entropy settings.
01054. **WebSocket message-schema inference** — record request/response frame pairs and cluster shapes since inferred schemas reveal undocumented message types.
01055. **WebSocket binary-frame handling test** — send binary and text frames interchangeably because mixed-frame parsers often have deserialization gaps.
01056. **WebSocket compression abuse check** — negotiate permessage-deflate and send highly compressible payloads since compression can amplify memory usage per connection.
01057. **WebSocket max-frame-size probe** — send growing frames to find truncation points because oversized-frame handling reveals parser limits.
01058. **WebSocket ping/pong behavior map** — measure keepalive timeouts and pong requirements since idle-connection policies determine hijack windows.
01059. **WebSocket reconnection-token analysis** — capture resume tokens across reconnects because predictable resume tokens let attackers take over sessions.
01060. **WebSocket message-ordering assumption test** — send out-of-order dependent messages since servers assuming order may apply operations to wrong state.
01061. **GraphQL subscription handshake test** — open graphql-ws connections with varied auth payloads because subscription transports often validate auth differently than HTTP.
01062. **Server-Sent Events endpoint discovery** — probe /events, /stream and text/event-stream content types since SSE endpoints stream privileged updates with weak auth.
01063. **SSE event-type enumeration** — catalog event: field values because event types reveal internal workflows like payments and moderation.
01064. **SSE Last-Event-ID replay test** — replay old event IDs since servers may re-emit historical events containing other users' data.
01065. **Long-polling endpoint discovery** — detect hanging GET patterns on /poll and /updates because long-poll endpoints bypass standard request logging.
01066. **API version path enumeration** — brute-force /v1, /v2, /v3, /beta, /internal, /canary prefixes since old versions stay live with weaker validation.
01067. **API version header negotiation** — test Accept-version, X-API-Version and vendor MIME types because header-versioned APIs hide entire version surfaces.
01068. **API version query-param test** — try ?version=2 and ?apiVersion= across endpoints since param-versioned routes bypass path-based WAF rules.
01069. **API version subdomain sweep** — probe v2.api., api-v2. and beta-api. hosts because version subdomains often point at staging stacks.
01070. **Old-version security regression diff** — compare auth checks between v1 and v2 since deprecated versions routinely miss newer authorization fixes.
01071. **Old-version field-exposure diff** — diff response schemas across versions because retired versions frequently return fields later removed for privacy.
01072. **Beta endpoint weak-validation hypothesis** — fuzz beta paths harder than stable ones since beta code ships with looser input validation.

## J. Business-logic flaws (price, workflow, coupon, referral abuse)

02997. **Currency-switch price arbitrage** — switch checkout currency mid-session to exploit stale exchange-rate caches and pay less in a weaker currency.
02998. **Negative-quantity cart injection** — submit negative quantities so line-item math subtracts value and shrinks the order total.
02999. **Fractional-quantity rounding exploit** — add 0.5 or 0.1 quantities where the backend truncates decimals, underpaying per unit.
03000. **Client-side total override** — tamper the `total` field in the checkout POST because the server trusts client-calculated amounts.
03001. **Unit-price field tampering** — replay the add-to-cart request with a modified `price` parameter the server never re-validates.
03002. **Decimal-truncation at capture** — authorize $10.99 but capture $10.9 by exploiting float truncation between authorize and capture calls.
03003. **Price parameter in redirect URL** — alter the price embedded in payment-gateway redirect URLs that lack server-side verification.
03004. **Zero-price variant selection** — select a product variant whose price resolves to null or 0 when the variant ID is forged.
03005. **Currency-mismatch refund arbitrage** — pay in one currency and refund in another, profiting from rate drift between the two operations.
03006. **Discount-then-currency flip** — apply a percentage coupon in a high-value currency then switch locale so the absolute discount converts wrongly.
03007. **Tax-inclusive versus exclusive confusion** — toggle region so tax is treated as included then excluded, shaving the tax amount off the total.
03008. **Shipping-included price leak** — buy items priced with bundled shipping then switch to in-store pickup to pocket the shipping margin.
03009. **Bulk-tier boundary gaming** — add N+1 items so tier pricing recalculates the whole cart cheaper, then remove the extra item.
03010. **Price-freeze via stale cart** — keep an old cart session alive across a price increase so checkout honors the cached lower price.
03011. **Sale-plus-membership stacking** — combine a sale price with a member-tier discount that were never meant to compose.
03012. **Gift-wrap fee nullification** — set gift-wrap quantity high while its price field is tamperable, driving the total negative.
03013. **Add-on SKU price replay** — capture a $0 promotional add-on SKU and replay it on later orders after the promo ends.
03014. **Multi-currency wallet debit** — pay with a wallet denominated in currency A while the order is priced in B, exploiting the internal conversion rate.
03015. **Display-versus-charge drift** — the frontend shows a rounded price while the backend charges the unrounded value across currencies.
03016. **Pre-tax versus post-tax coupon** — reorder the calculation pipeline via parameter flags so discounts apply to the tax-inclusive base.
03017. **Negative discount injection** — pass a negative discount value that the backend adds instead of subtracting.
03018. **Free-shipping threshold manipulation** — inflate the cart with removable items to cross the free-shipping threshold, then remove them post-lock.
03019. **Localized price-list confusion** — request a region with lower list prices via header spoofing while shipping to a high-price region.
03020. **Price-match guarantee abuse** — submit a forged competitor price for an inflated item and collect the match plus loyalty points.
03021. **Introductory pricing retrigger** — cycle through plan changes that each re-trigger first-month introductory pricing.
03022. **Metered-usage under-reporting** — tamper the client-side usage beacon so metered billing counts fewer API calls or seats.
03023. **Overage rounding-down** — consume 1.9 overage units where the billing job floors to 1, systematically underpaying overages.
03024. **Price-drop adjustment looping** — buy before a sale, then trigger the price-adjustment policy repeatedly across overlapping windows.
03025. **Flash-sale cache lag** — hit the CDN-cached sale price after the sale ends because cache invalidation lags the price change.
03026. **Bundle component substitution** — swap a bundle's expensive component for a cheap one via the customize endpoint while keeping the bundle price.
03027. **Cross-border tax exemption fraud** — set a VAT-exempt business flag with an unvalidated VAT ID to strip tax from consumer orders.
03028. **Employee-discount code sharing** — brute-force or share single-use employee discount codes that lack per-user binding.
03029. **Student-discount verification bypass** — complete verification with disposable credentials then reuse the discount indefinitely.
03030. **Quote-to-order price lock** — modify the cart between the price-quote and order-commit steps to lock a lower quoted price.
03031. **Donation-amount perk unlock** — enter negative or zero donations tied to donor perks, unlocking perks without paying.
03032. **Dynamic-pricing context probing** — query the pricing engine with crafted contexts (location, device, time) to discover the minimum-price combination and replay it at checkout.
03033. **Coupon stacking via multiple fields** — apply one code in `coupon` and another in `promo_code` fields that validate independently.
03034. **Coupon reuse via case mutation** — redeem the same single-use code with different casing when comparison is case-sensitive but redemption is not.
03035. **Coupon reuse across accounts** — redeem a one-per-customer code on multiple accounts sharing one email alias.
03036. **Expired-coupon timezone replay** — use a code past expiry by hitting a region server still inside the valid window.
03037. **Coupon brute-force with prefix** — enumerate predictable coupon formats (e.g., SUMMER-XXXX) using the known prefix and checksum pattern.
03038. **Referral-code as coupon** — enter another user's referral code in the coupon field where both draw from the same validation table.
03039. **Gift-card code as coupon** — submit gift-card codes to the coupon endpoint that accepts any stored-value code type.
03040. **Coupon applied to gift cards** — buy gift cards with a coupon where terms forbid it, because cart-level discounts don't exclude stored-value SKUs.
03041. **Minimum-spend bypass** — add a gift card to reach the coupon's minimum spend, then the discount applies to the whole cart.
03042. **Shipping coupon on digital goods** — apply shipping coupons to digital-only carts to trigger fallback discounts that zero the total.
03043. **Over-value coupon credit** — use a fixed-amount coupon exceeding the cart total where no zero-floor turns the remainder into store credit.
03044. **Coupon reactivation after cancel** — cancel an order that consumed a single-use coupon and get the coupon reissued without invalidation.
03045. **Draft-order coupon cloning** — create multiple draft orders each locking the same single-use coupon before any converts.
03046. **Coupon on renewal invoices** — apply a first-order-only coupon to recurring renewals that reuse the initial order's discount snapshot.
03047. **Affiliate coupon self-attribution** — apply your own affiliate coupon to earn both the discount and the affiliate commission.
03048. **Coupon leakage via errors** — the validation endpoint reveals whether a code exists versus is expired, enabling oracle-based enumeration.
03049. **Timing-based coupon validation** — response-time differences between valid, invalid, and expired codes enable enumeration without rate limits.
03050. **Coupon region-lock bypass** — redeem a region-locked code by spoofing the billing country at redemption time.
03051. **BOGO on single item** — trigger buy-one-get-one logic with quantity 1 where the free item grants without the paid-counterpart check.
03052. **Percentage coupon on fees** — apply percentage coupons to non-discountable fees via line-item targeting parameters.
03053. **Coupon inheritance via share-link** — the share-cart link embeds the coupon so anyone opening it inherits a single-use discount.
03054. **Employee coupon reverse-engineering** — reverse the coupon-generation algorithm from observed codes to mint valid new ones.
03055. **Post-payment coupon injection** — inject a coupon into the post-payment adjustment endpoint that recalculates and refunds the difference.
03056. **Split-order coupon multiplication** — split one cart into N orders to apply a per-order coupon N times on the same items.
03057. **Price-match plus coupon dip** — combine an approved price-match adjustment with a coupon that should have been voided.
03058. **Points-to-coupon conversion loop** — convert points to coupons at a favorable rate, then refund the points-earning order while keeping the coupon.
03059. **Coupon on pre-order deposit** — apply full-value coupons to a small pre-order deposit, shrinking the balance due disproportionately.
03060. **Abandoned-cart coupon farming** — repeatedly abandon carts with throwaway emails to harvest unique retargeting coupons.
03061. **Welcome-coupon rotation** — re-register with email aliases to collect unlimited new-customer coupons.
03062. **Locale-switched coupon eligibility** — switch storefront locale to one where the coupon's terms render incorrectly, bypassing client-side eligibility checks.
03063. **Minimum-quantity bypass** — meet "buy 3 get 20% off" with 3 items then remove 2 in the same request batch the validator misses.
03064. **Cross-platform coupon stacking** — apply a mobile-only and a web-only coupon to the same synced account cart.
03065. **Tax-base coupon toggle** — force the discount onto the pre-tax versus post-tax subtotal by toggling the tax-display setting mid-checkout.
03066. **Self-referral discount use** — use your own referral link's discount on your own account when attribution checks only the code.
03067. **Coupon resurrection after refund** — refund an order and the coupon returns to the pool because the redemption record is deleted, not flagged.
03068. **Flash-coupon cache window** — redeem a limited-quantity coupon in the gap between campaign end and cache refresh.
03069. **Self-referral loop** — refer yourself with a second account and collect both the referrer reward and the referee bonus.
03070. **Referral cookie stuffing** — plant referral cookies via hidden iframes so organic signups attribute to your affiliate account.
03071. **Multi-account referral farming** — script account creation behind rotating emails to harvest per-referral payouts at scale.
03072. **Referral on existing users** — trigger the referral reward on pre-existing accounts by backdating the attribution event.
03073. **Affiliate self-purchase commission** — route your own purchases through your affiliate link where self-purchase isn't excluded.
03074. **Fake conversion injection** — fire the affiliate postback pixel directly with forged order IDs to mint commissions.
03075. **Attribution window extension** — modify the referral cookie expiry client-side where the server trusts the cookie's timestamp.
03076. **Last-click attribution theft** — overwrite a legitimate affiliate's cookie at checkout with your own via a link shortener.
03077. **Referral tier escalation** — game tiered affiliate payouts by cycling fake volume to reach higher commission brackets.
03078. **Sub-affiliate pyramid cut** — register fake sub-affiliates to siphon override commissions without real downstream sales.
03079. **Referral credit cashout** — convert non-cash referral credits into cash-equivalent gift cards through the rewards catalog.
03080. **Chargeback-proof referral** — earn referral payouts on orders you later charge back, where clawback logic doesn't cover referrals.
03081. **Referral campaign tampering** — alter the campaign ID in your referral link to attribute sales to a higher-paying campaign.
03082. **Deep-link referral hijack** — share deep links carrying your referral code into in-app purchases the merchant thought unattributable.
03083. **QR-code referral swap** — replace a merchant's in-store referral QR with your own to harvest walk-in attributions.
03084. **Disposable-domain referee farming** — use catch-all email domains to mass-create referee accounts that pass verification.
03085. **Payout-threshold gaming** — split earnings across accounts to stay under manual-review payout thresholds.
03086. **Fake install attribution** — spoof mobile attribution SDK events to claim install bounties for installs that never happened.

03091. **Dormancy-purge evasion** — keep farmed referee accounts active with scripted logins to dodge dormancy purges.

03121. **Paid-refunded-reshipped cycle** — refund an order then use the "reship missing item" flow to get the goods again without paying.

03126. **Pause-resume billing gap** — pause a subscription to stop billing while the grace period keeps features active, then resume cyclically.
03127. **Trial-to-paid state confusion** — cancel during trial but keep the paid entitlement because the state machine leaves the grant active.
03128. **Dispute-plus-refund** — open a payment dispute and simultaneously request a merchant refund, collecting both.

## K. Race conditions & concurrency attacks

03331. **Coupon double-redeem** — fire parallel coupon-redemption requests so both pass the single-use check before either commits.
03332. **Balance double-debit** — send concurrent withdrawal requests that each see the pre-debit balance and both succeed.
03333. **Credit-spend race** — spend the same store credit on two checkouts simultaneously before the ledger updates.
03334. **OTP single-use bypass** — submit the same OTP in parallel requests before the first consumes it.
03335. **Password-reset token reuse** — use a reset token twice concurrently before invalidation commits.
03336. **Invite-code multi-redeem** — redeem a single-use invite link from parallel sessions.
03337. **Promo-claim race** — claim a limited-quantity promo concurrently to exceed the stock cap.
03338. **Seat-hold race** — hold the same seat from two sessions where the hold check isn't atomic.
03339. **Voucher redemption race** — redeem the same voucher code twice in the same millisecond window.
03340. **Points-redeem race** — redeem loyalty points for rewards twice before the balance decrements.
03341. **Withdrawal-limit race** — exceed daily withdrawal limits with parallel requests that each check the limit independently.
03342. **Ticket-purchase race** — buy more tickets than the per-user cap via concurrent purchases.
03343. **Refund-request race** — submit duplicate refund requests that each pass the "not yet refunded" check.
03344. **Top-up webhook race** — exploit top-up webhooks arriving twice to credit the wallet twice.
03345. **API-quota race** — exceed rate limits by bursting requests that increment the counter non-atomically.
03346. **Email-swap verification dodge** — change the account email concurrently to bypass verification of the new address.
03347. **Username-claim race** — register the same username simultaneously where uniqueness is checked before insert.
03348. **Auction-bid increment race** — place concurrent bids that both pass the minimum-increment check against the same base price.
03349. **Poll-vote race** — vote twice before the has-voted flag persists.
03350. **File-upload quota race** — upload files concurrently to exceed storage quotas checked per-request.
03351. **Subscription-cancel race** — cancel and resubscribe concurrently to land in an inconsistent billing state.
03352. **Gift-card redeem race** — redeem the same gift card on two orders before the balance updates.
03353. **Deposit-bonus race** — trigger a deposit bonus twice with concurrent deposits where the bonus check isn't locked.
03354. **Cashback-claim race** — claim cashback on the same order from two sessions.
03355. **Leaderboard-score race** — submit scores concurrently to double-count a single achievement.

## L. JWT / OAuth / OIDC / SAML attacks

03664. **alg-none acceptance** — strip the signature and set alg to none where the verifier honors it.
03665. **RS256-to-HS256 confusion** — sign an RS256 token with the public key as the HMAC secret.
03666. **HS256-to-RS256 confusion** — trick the verifier into the reverse confusion via ambiguous key handling.
03667. **Duplicate alg header** — add a duplicate alg claim where the parser reads the first and the verifier the second.
03668. **Case-variant alg** — use "None", "NONE", or "nOnE" where the comparison is case-sensitive downstream.
03669. **alg confusion via jku** — combine a malicious jku with alg HS256 to supply your own HMAC key.
03670. **Empty-signature bypass** — send a token with an empty signature segment where the verifier skips empty signatures.
03671. **Signature stripping** — remove the third segment entirely; some parsers treat the token as valid.
03672. **alg-none with kid** — include a kid pointing to a null key to satisfy key lookup with none.
03673. **Mixed-alg chains** — chain tokens where the gateway checks alg but the backend doesn't.
03674. **none-alg in nested JWT** — hide alg:none in an inner nested JWT the outer verifier doesn't inspect.
03675. **Algorithm allowlist bypass** — use "HS384" where the allowlist checks only the prefix "HS256".
03676. **none with trailing data** — append data after the signature; the verifier truncates before checking alg.
03677. **kid plus none** — the key-ID lookup returns empty, and empty keys are treated as "no verification."
03678. **x5c with none** — embed a self-signed x5c chain alongside alg:none to confuse validators.
03679. **EdDSA-to-HMAC confusion** — confusion between EdDSA and HMAC where the key material is reused.
03680. **PS256-to-HS256 downgrade** — downgrade RSASSA-PSS to HMAC using the RSA public key.
03681. **JWKS alg mismatch** — the JWKS advertises RS256 but the token uses HS256 with the same key ID.
03682. **none in refresh tokens** — refresh tokens accept alg:none even when access tokens don't.
03683. **none in WebSocket** — the WebSocket auth path skips algorithm checks the HTTP path enforces.
03684. **none in query param** — tokens passed as ?token= accept none where the header path doesn't.
03685. **Legacy-verifier confusion** — a legacy microservice behind the gateway still accepts none after re-signing.
03686. **SAML-derived JWT confusion** — apply alg:none to tokens parsed from SAML assertions by JWT libraries.
03687. **Certificate-as-HMAC-secret** — use the X.509 certificate bytes as the HMAC secret.
03688. **Octet-key confusion** — supply a JWK with kty:oct where the server expected RSA.
03689. **Federation symmetric confusion** — an IdP-issued HS256 token accepted by an RS256-only relying party.
03690. **cty parser switch** — use the content-type header to switch the parser into an unverified mode.
03691. **none in embedded tokens** — tokens embedded in URLs for passwordless login accept alg:none.
03692. **jku SSRF key injection** — point jku at an attacker server to supply the verification key.
03693. **jku DNS rebinding** — serve a malicious JWKS via DNS rebinding to bypass jku allowlists.
03694. **x5u certificate injection** — point x5u at an attacker certificate the verifier trusts without pinning.
03695. **x5u path traversal** — use file:// or path traversal in x5u to load a local key file.
03696. **jku allowlist bypass** — bypass the jku domain allowlist with a subdomain or redirect.
03697. **jku redirect** — the jku URL 301-redirects to an attacker domain after allowlist validation.
03698. **x5u redirect** — validate the original x5u URL, then follow its redirect to the attacker domain.
03699. **JWKS cache poisoning** — replace the JWKS endpoint's keys via cache poisoning so your key verifies.
03700. **JWKS kid collision** — publish a JWKS with a colliding kid the verifier prefers over the real one.
03701. **jku parameter pollution** — supply two jku headers; the allowlist checks one, the fetcher uses the other.
03702. **x5c self-signed trust** — embed a self-signed x5c chain where the verifier doesn't check the trust anchor.
03703. **jku file inclusion** — jku with file:// URLs probes local key material via error messages.
03704. **x5u LDAP exfiltration** — x5u pointing at an LDAP URL exfiltrates data in Java validators.
03705. **jku slow-server** — point jku at a slow server to hang verifiers that fail open on timeout.

## M. Cloud misconfig (S3, Azure, GCP, Firebase — new check types)

03995. **Bucket policy versus object ACL differential** — probe ListObjects and GetObject anonymously and under spoofed Referer identities to flag objects whose ACLs are wider than the bucket policy implies, catching "private" buckets that leak individual files.
03996. **ListBucket error-code oracle** — compare AccessDenied, NoSuchBucket, and AllAccessDisabled responses to confirm bucket existence without brute force, feeding a reliable existence oracle into deeper ACL probes.
03997. **S3 XML error differential mapper** — parse Error/Code values across guessed keys to distinguish forbidden-existing objects from nonexistent ones, enabling targeted content discovery instead of blind guessing.
03998. **READ_ACP grant scanner** — request ?acl on discovered buckets and objects to detect AllUsers or authenticated-users READ_ACP grants that expose the full permission graph to anyone.
03999. **Bucket version enumeration** — list ?versions on versioned buckets to recover deleted or overwritten objects such as old .env files and backups that owners assume are gone.
04000. **Delete-marker bypass retrieval** — request specific VersionIds sitting beneath delete markers to resurrect "deleted" secrets from versioned buckets.
04001. **S3 Select expression injection probe** — test select-object-content endpoints for expression injection that reads objects outside the intended prefix.
04002. **Wildcard principal policy detector** — fetch ?policy and flag Principal "*" paired with s3:GetObject on sensitive prefixes like backups/ or *.sql.
04003. **Cross-account confused-deputy tester** — check whether bucket policies trusting another account's role can be triggered by unauthenticated writes that the trusted account later processes.
04004. **MFA-delete gap flagger** — read versioning configuration to flag crown-jewel buckets lacking MFADelete, the precondition for silent destructive wipes.
04005. **Object-lock retention bypass probe** — test PutObjectRetention downgrades on compliance-mode objects to see whether supposedly immutable backups can actually be rewritten.
04006. **Presigned URL parameter tampering** — mutate X-Amz-Expires, X-Amz-SignedHeaders, and response-content-disposition on leaked presigned URLs to extend or repurpose their access.
04007. **Presigned POST policy forgery test** — decode leaked POST policies, then test widened conditions like starts-with key and content-length-range to upload attacker content into the victim bucket.
04008. **Presigned URL log mining** — extract presigned URLs from JS bundles, traffic captures, and public repos, then replay them for direct object reads the frontend never intended.
04009. **S3 Access Point policy gap probe** — enumerate S3 Access Points and Object Lambda endpoints whose own policies may be looser than the backing bucket's policy.
04010. **Directory bucket endpoint checks** — probe s3express endpoints for objects whose single-AZ storage and distinct policies diverge from the account's standard buckets.
04011. **Bucket CORS wildcard theft test** — test CORS rules with an attacker Origin plus credentials to confirm cross-site theft of "private" objects through victim browsers.

## P. Mobile backend / IoT / hardware-adjacent tests

04995. **App-version header down-negotiation probe** — send requests with legacy X-App-Version values to detect whether old mobile builds hit unpatched endpoints and receive less-strict authorization.
04996. **Mobile-only endpoint inventory via forced headers** — replay the web API with typical mobile headers (X-Device-Model, X-OS-Version) to uncover endpoints that only activate for app clients.
04997. **App-version floor bypass by date rollback** — spoof an ancient build timestamp in version headers to see if server-side minimum-version enforcement can be dodged without updating.
04998. **Certificate pinning test report generator** — document whether the backend rejects connections from a non-pinned test harness and produce a pinning-effectiveness report for the client.
04999. **Deep-link scheme parameter tamper probe** — replay app deep links (myapp://path?param=) against the backend to find authorization decisions that trust client-side routing parameters.
05000. **Universal-link assetlinks.json gap scan** — verify that /.well-known/assetlinks.json actually restricts claimed domains to the real app package and flag wildcard or debug fingerprints.
05001. **Apple-app-site-association drift check** — compare the live apple-app-site-association file against the shipping app to catch universal-link claims the current build no longer supports.
05002. **Push-notification endpoint impersonation test** — attempt to register a fake device token against the push registration endpoint to see if sender identity is verified before messages queue.
05003. **Push payload injection to unregistered tokens** — send malformed push tokens to the notification API and watch for verbose errors that leak internal queue or provider credentials.
05004. **Device-enrollment replay with cloned identifiers** — enroll two virtual devices sharing one device fingerprint to detect missing uniqueness enforcement on device identity.
05005. **Provisioning profile quota exhaustion test** — flood the device-provisioning endpoint to check whether enrollment quotas exist or a single account can spawn unlimited devices.
05006. **OTP-via-SMS gateway logic flaw probe** — request OTPs with mismatched phone-number formatting variants to find normalization bugs that route codes to attacker-controlled numbers.
05007. **OTP resend throttle bypass via channel flip** — alternate between SMS, voice, and WhatsApp OTP channels to test whether rate limits are tracked per channel instead of per account.
05008. **Play Integrity verdict spoofing detection test** — submit tampered integrity tokens to the backend and verify the server actually validates them against Google's API instead of trusting the payload.
05009. **App Attest receipt validation probe** — send App Attest attestations with manipulated nonce values to check whether the server binds receipts to the current challenge.
05010. **Attestation failure open-vs-closed gate test** — disable attestation in a test build and observe whether the backend fails closed (deny) or fails open (allow degraded access).
05011. **IoT default credential safe-check dictionary** — probe device login APIs with a curated list of vendor defaults using a single safe attempt per device and stop on first success to avoid lockouts.
05012. **MQTT broker exposure scanner** — test whether the MQTT broker port is internet-reachable without client certificates and report accessible system topics.
05013. **MQTT topic wildcard enumeration** — subscribe to multi-level wildcards on the authorized test account's broker to detect topics leaking other users' device telemetry.
05014. **MQTT retained-message leak audit** — read retained messages on public topics to find credentials, tokens, or firmware URLs left in retained payloads.
05015. **CoAP resource discovery probe** — query /.well-known/core on device endpoints to enumerate exposed CoAP resources and test which accept unauthenticated POST.
05016. **CoAP observe subscription hijack test** — register observe callbacks on another device's resources using the test tenant's credentials to detect missing CoAP authorization.
05017. **Firmware-update endpoint hijack simulation** — request the OTA manifest with a downgraded version to verify the device or backend rejects unsigned or older firmware images.
05018. **Firmware manifest signature validation probe** — tamper the OTA manifest's checksum field to test whether the update pipeline verifies integrity before serving binaries.
05019. **Firmware binary URL prediction test** — mutate version strings in firmware download URLs to see if unreleased or internal builds are fetchable without authentication.
05020. **BLE-adjacent backend API replay probe** — capture BLE-gateway API calls from the companion app and replay them with modified device MACs to test gateway-side binding.
05021. **BLE pairing-code backend brute-force guard test** — measure lockout behavior on the pairing-code verification endpoint to confirm rate limiting exists per device rather than per IP.
05022. **AWS IoT device-shadow cross-tenant read** — request another device's shadow document using the test tenant's policy to verify IAM policies isolate device shadows.
05023. **Device-shadow desired-state injection** — push a malicious desired state to a shadow and check whether the twin service validates state payloads before devices consume them.
05024. **Mobile analytics key abuse check** — replay analytics SDK keys from a decompiled app against the ingestion endpoint to test whether keys are validated per app bundle.
05025. **Analytics event schema poisoning probe** — submit out-of-schema analytics events to detect backend crashes or log-injection paths in the ingestion pipeline.
05026. **In-app-purchase receipt validation bypass test** — submit forged Apple/Google receipts to the purchase-verification endpoint and check whether the server validates signatures with the store.
05027. **IAP receipt replay across accounts** — redeem the same valid receipt under a second test account to detect missing one-time-use enforcement on consumables.
05028. **Subscription entitlement downgrade probe** — cancel a sandbox subscription then keep calling premium APIs to verify entitlements revoke promptly server-side.
05029. **Mobile feature-flag endpoint enumeration** — query the flags endpoint without authentication to map unreleased features and their kill-switch conditions.
05030. **Feature-flag override header test** — send X-Feature-Override headers to force-enable gated features and check whether the backend trusts client-side flag state.
05031. **QR-code backend flow token capture** — scan app QR pairing flows and replay the embedded one-time tokens twice to test single-use enforcement.
05032. **QR login session fixation probe** — generate a QR login code, let it sit, then complete it from a second device to test expiry and binding to the originating session.
05033. **NFC-triggered backend action replay** — replay NFC tag payloads (ndef records) against the tag-action API to find actions executable without physical tag presence.

## R. PoC generation (auto-exploit chains, video PoCs, interactive demos)

05661. **One-click XSS exploit page builder** — generate a self-contained HTML page that fires the reflected XSS payload on load for instant client-side demonstration.
05662. **CSRF one-click demo page** — build an auto-submitting form page that replays the state-changing request to prove missing CSRF protection.
05663. **Clickjacking overlay demo** — generate a transparent-iframe overlay page showing how UI redressing tricks a victim into clicking a privileged button.
05664. **Tabnabbing PoC page** — create a demo page that opens the target with window.opener access to prove reverse-tabnabbing impact.
05665. **Collaborator-style OOB interaction proof** — embed unique canary URLs in payloads and auto-correlate inbound hits to prove blind SSRF/XXE/RCE.
